questions.text: In a healthy young adult male, the normal average Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) is approximately:

options.A: 125 mL/min (180 Liters per day)
options.B: 650 mL/min (equal to renal plasma flow)
options.C: 50 mL/min (70 Liters per day)
options.D: 1200 mL/min (equal to renal blood flow)
options.E: 1 to 2 mL/min (equal to urine flow rate)

questions.explanation:
**Starling Forces & Net**: volume is reabsorbed along the nephron, yielding ~ 1-1.5 L/day final urine. mL/min requiring dialysis or transplant). Filtration equilibrium occurs when pi_gc rises to equal (Pgc - Pbs), Pgc ~50-55 mmHg (favors, constant along loop). Pbs ~15-18 mmHg (opposes). pi_gc ~28->36 mmHg (opposes, rises progressively as protein halting ultrafiltration before blood exits into the efferent arteriole (seen

**Filtration Pressure (NFP)**: concentrates). pi_bs ~0 mmHg. NFP = (Pgc - Pbs) - (pi_gc - pi_bs) = ~10 at low plasma flow states).
